summary: Today’s pulse tracks US envoys hold talks with Zelensky in Kyiv after meeting Putin, China prepares £40bn stimulus for financial sector amid fears over sluggish growth, and Shoebridge criticises Labor response after IDF officer’s ‘reprehensible’ comments on deadly Zomi Frankcom strike. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are financial, flights, and group. In the background, Volcanic eruption halts flights at Jakarta and seven other Indonesian airports and Black-clad Dover vigilantes will return if police do not act, say campaigners keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: US envoys hold talks with Zelensky in Kyiv after meeting Putin
headlines.description: Steve Witkoff tells reporters the US team feels "encouraged" by a "substantive" and important discussion.

headlines.title: China prepares £40bn stimulus for financial sector amid fears over sluggish growth
headlines.description: Beijing wants banks and insurers to bolster investment in stock market as it helps to replenish cash reserves China will inject $54bn (£40bn) into its financial sector as Beijing attempts to shore up banks and insurers in the face of faltering economic growth. A host of financial institutions said they were due to receive billions of yuan in capital from state institutions including the ministry of finance and even the company that runs the country’s tobacco monopoly.

headlines.title: Shoebridge criticises Labor response after IDF officer’s ‘reprehensible’ comments on deadly Zomi Frankcom strike
headlines.description: Greens defence spokesman says ‘words are just distractions’ until government takes action ‘Guilt by association’: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike Australian aid worker Frankcom and six of her colleagues were killed in 2024 while bringing food to the people of Gaza . Former IDF reserve colonel Nochi Mendel has said he would do “exactly the same thing” again and that those killed in the World Central Kitchen (WCK) humanitarian convoy in Gaza were “not innocent”.

headlines.title: Volcanic eruption halts flights at Jakarta and seven other Indonesian airports
headlines.description: Ash cloud from Anak Krakatau affects hundreds of flights and some school and fishing activities Indonesia halted operations at eight airports on Sunday, including from its main international hub, affecting hundreds of flights as a result of an ash cloud from the Anak Krakatau volcano. Saturday’s eruption, which produced lava and booming sounds that were heard up to 435 miles (700km) away, according to Indonesia’s geology agency, also interrupted some school activities and fishing.

headlines.title: Black-clad Dover vigilantes will return if police do not act, say campaigners
headlines.description: Far-right linked group able to mobilise at scale due to police ‘inaction’, says founder of Hope Not Hate The group of masked, black-clad vigilantes who blockaded roads in Dover could repeat the disruption unless police step up efforts to stop them, politicians and campaigners have said. Responsibility for the demonstration has been claimed by Patriot Platform, an anti-immigration group with links to the far right, which styles itself as having a “fierce love for our homeland”.

headlines.title: Dozens feared trapped in collapsed building in Delhi
headlines.description: As many as 50 people are thought to have been inside the five-storey hostel when it came down.

headlinePool.title: No bailouts for Jaguar Land Rover amid reports of thousands of job cuts, says minister
headlinePool.description: Carmaker, which is battling Trump tariffs and Chinese competitors, faces talks with union leaders and government The government has signalled that it will not invest taxpayers’ money to limit job losses at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), after it emerged that the UK’s biggest carmaker is planning up to 4,000 redundancies . Before crunch talks on Tuesday between JLR, union leaders and government officials, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said it was not his job to “intervene and run businesses”.

headlinePool.title: German startup sends first commercial rocket into space from Europe
headlinePool.description: Isar Aerospace plans rapid expansion amid race to capitalise on expanding satellite-launch market A German startup has launched the first commercial rocket to reach orbit from continental Europe, a milestone for Europe’s efforts to secure independent access to space. Isar Aerospace said on Sunday that it would rapidly ⁠expand satellite deployments after the ⁠first orbital launch of ​its uncrewed Spectrum rocket from Arctic Norway, marking a ⁠breakthrough for a region where several countries are seeking a foothold in the fast-growing market for satellite launches.

headlinePool.title: US envoys Kushner and Witkoff arrive in Kyiv after talks with Putin
headlinePool.description: Arrival marks first visit to Ukraine and comes day after ‘substantive plans’ on ending war discussed in Moscow The US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Kyiv for a second day of talks on how to end the war in Ukraine. Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, met the pair in Sophia Square, in front of Kyiv’s historic Saint Sophia Cathedral. Zelenskyy greeted Witkoff with a hug, saying: “It’s good to see you, Steve.”

headlinePool.title: Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles
headlinePool.description: Slavery’s legacy continues ‘to deprive our country and our people’, says minister, as group prepares to appeal to Jamaica’s head of state A landmark petition is to be handed to King Charles by Jamaica over slavery reparations, aiming to confront historical crimes that still disadvantage former British colonies, the Caribbean nation’s culture minister has said. The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.

headlinePool.title: Undercover report on donations ‘looks bad’ for Reform, admits Nigel Farage – as it happened
headlinePool.description: The Reform UK leader is under pressure after senior aides appeared to plot how to bypass electoral laws on foreign donations Sagal Abdi-Wali arrived in Camden as a child refugee from Somalia. She has worked for more than a decade as a volunteer and trustee for local charities and is a governor of two schools in the borough, according to Labour. She was first elected as a councillor in 2022 and became the leader of the council in May, when she said: “Camden has been my home for 35 years. It is the place that gave my family sanctuary, that welcomed us, and that has shaped so much of who I am, what I stand for and what inspired my commitment to public service and to working for the community that welcomed us.”

headlinePool.title: Zia Yusuf’s post about Camden council leader is ‘straightforward racism’, says minister
headlinePool.description: Senior Reform UK figure has faced criticism within party after post about Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee Labour has accused Reform’s Zia Yusuf of “straightforward racism” after he suggested the party’s frontrunner to replace Keir Starmer in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection was not British. Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee from Somalia and the leader of Camden council, has been tipped as an early favourite to contest the London seat for Labour after the former prime minister’s resignation.

headlinePool.title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong
headlinePool.description: As the UN adopts a new world map to reflect Africa's true size, let's take a closer look at what different maps get right and wrong.

headlinePool.title: Canadian skyrunner goes missing during training session for Matterhorn record attempt
headlinePool.description: Kalie McCrystal was hoping to break record in Alps Athlete was last seen on Tuesday afternoon Canadian athlete Kalie McCrystal has gone missing during preparations for a record attempt in the Alps. McCrystal, from Squamish in British Columbia, was on a “reconnaissance/training session” in the run-up to her attempt at ascending and descending the 14,692 ft (4,478m) Matterhorn on the Swiss-Italian border.

headlinePool.description: "We achieved within a few years what had taken the European space industry decades before."
